patients.summary: Data entry specialist with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, mixed hyperlipidemia and obesity who joined in 2021; acanthosis nigricans, pes anserinus pain, tarsal tunnel syndrome, NASH, endometrial hyperplasia and a hepatic adenoma follow. A 2026 laparoscopic hysterectomy is complicated by a small-bowel perforation repaired at an outside hospital.

New pt appt booked 9/14 8:40 AM. Asked to bring pill bottles and come fasting. Records release form emailed, she will sign and return.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

52 yo woman here to establish care. Previous primary office no longer takes her plan. Records requested.

HPI: Type 2 diabetes for several years, on metformin 1000 mg BID, no other agent ever. Also HTN on lisinopril 20 and high cholesterol/triglycerides on atorvastatin 40. Says she used to see an endocrinologist alongside her old PCP, last went in the spring, not planning to go back if we can manage it here. No home glucose meter in use ("the strips ran out"). Takes meds most days. No polyuria, polydipsia, vision change, chest pain, dyspnea, foot sores. Weight has been about the same for years.

PMH: T2DM, HTN, mixed hyperlipidemia, obesity.
PSH: laparoscopic cholecystectomy 2014.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother T2DM. Father HTN and high cholesterol. Maternal grandmother endometrial cancer.
SH: data entry specialist, sits most of the day. Never smoker. No alcohol. No drugs. Lives in Easthampton.
GYN: still having periods, regular. Pap and mammogram done at old office, will confirm from records.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: Vitals as recorded. BMI 35.
Gen: well appearing, pleasant.
HEENT: normal. Neck supple, no thyromegaly.
CV: RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear.
Abd: obese, soft, nontender, healed laparoscopic port scars.
Ext: no edema. Feet: skin intact, pulses 2+, monofilament intact bilaterally.
Psych: normal mood and affect.

A/P:
1. T2DM - not at goal by her report. A1c today. Diet basics reviewed. Continue metformin. New meter and strips sent.
2. HTN - above goal today. Continue lisinopril 20, recheck next visit.
3. Mixed hyperlipidemia - continue atorvastatin 40, lipids today.
4. Obesity - talked about walking at lunch.
5. HM - HIV screen today (never done). Records for Pap, colonoscopy, mammogram, vaccines. Flu shot when it arrives.

RTC 4 months, sooner with results.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Ms. Washington,

Your labs from Tuesday are back. Your A1c (3-month sugar average) is above where we want it, and your triglycerides are high. Kidney function, blood counts and the urine protein test look fine, and the HIV screen is negative.

For now: keep taking the metformin twice a day with meals, start using the new meter a few mornings a week, and try to cut back on sweet drinks. We will recheck at your next visit in January.

Your primary care physician

reports.text: Specimen: ThinPrep, cervical. Adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation, transformation zone present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.body:
Records received by fax from prior primary care office, 64 pages. Abstracted:
- Pap with HPV co-test 06/2020: negative / HPV not detected.
- Screening colonoscopy 05/2019: normal to cecum, no polyps, repeat in 10 years.
- Screening mammogram 02/2021: BI-RADS 1.
- Tdap 03/2018. COVID Pfizer x2 03/2021 and 04/2021.
- Problem list there: type 2 DM, HTN, hyperlipidemia, obesity. Notes mention co-management with an outside endocrinology office, last endo visit spring 2021.
- Meds match what she brought in.
Scanned to media. Routed to PCP.

orders.reason: darkening and thickening of skin of neck and axillae

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: F/u DM, HTN. Using the meter some mornings, fasting numbers 160s to 190s. Admits holidays were rough for diet. Taking all meds.
New: noticed the skin on the back of her neck and in both armpits getting darker and thicker since around late summer. Not itchy, not painful. Wants it looked at, worried it is a rash from deodorant.

O: Vitals as recorded. BMI ~35.
Skin: darkened, thickened skin at posterior neck and both axillae. No open areas.
CV RRR. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P:
1. T2DM - fasting labs today. Reinforced diet, walking. Continue metformin 1000 BID.
2. Skin change neck/axillae - send to dermatology for evaluation.
3. HTN - continue lisinopril.
4. Mixed hyperlipidemia - lipids today, continue atorvastatin.
5. Screening mammogram ordered (last 2/2021).

RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Results from Tuesday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Tammy - your A1c came back at 8.5 and your fasting sugar was 180, so the diabetes is running higher than we'd like. Cholesterol: LDL 145, triglycerides 250, HDL (the good one) 35. Kidney tests are fine.

Keep the metformin going and keep working on the food changes we talked about. The dermatology referral went out today; their office will call you. I also put in your mammogram order.

events.reason: darkening of skin of neck and axillae

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE DERMATOLOGY GROUP - CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 02/24/2022
Re: Tammy Washington, DOB 04/09/1969

Thank you for referring Ms. Washington. She describes about half a year of gradual darkening and thickening of the skin in both underarms and around the neck. No itching or pain. No new medications.

Her diabetes remains poorly controlled on metformin; we reviewed your January labs (A1c 8.5%, fasting glucose 180, total cholesterol 220, LDL 145, HDL 35, triglycerides 250). She also has hypertension. No family history of skin cancer. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BMI 35. Symmetric, hyperpigmented, velvety plaques of both axillae and the neck. No skin tags of concern, no other lesions examined of note.

Fasting insulin drawn today: 32 uIU/mL (high).

Impression: Acanthosis nigricans, consistent with insulin resistance.

Plan: The skin change reflects her insulin resistance and should soften with weight loss and better glucose control. No topical treatment needed at this point. Return as needed.

Dermatology

documents.title: Derm letter reviewed, call to patient
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Reviewed derm consult: acanthosis nigricans, fasting insulin 32. Added acanthosis and metabolic syndrome (obesity, TG 250, HDL 35, HTN, DM) to problem list.
Called pt, explained the skin change is from insulin resistance, not her deodorant. Same plan: food changes, more walking, metformin. She is going to try a lunchtime walk with a coworker. Mammogram scheduled for 3/23.

reports.text: Bilateral CC and MLO views. Comparison 02/2021. Scattered fibroglandular densities. No suspicious masses, calcifications or architectural distortion. No change.

documents.title: Mammogram result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Normal screening mammogram, BI-RADS 1. Letter to pt.

documents.title: knee
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, my right knee has been bothering me since around January. It's worse when I walk more (been trying the walks like you said lol) and better when I rest it. I didn't fall or twist it. Can I see a bone doctor? My insurance wants a referral. Thanks, Tammy

documents.title: RE: knee
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry to hear the knee is acting up just as you got going. Referral to orthopedics/sports medicine is in. Ice after walks and keep moving at a pace that doesn't hurt. If it swells, gets red or hot, or you can't bear weight, call us that day.

conditions.label: Pes anserinus bursitis of right knee

medications.sig: Apply 4 g to right knee up to 4 times daily as needed

reports.text: Right knee, 3 views. Mild joint space narrowing. No fracture or dislocation. No joint effusion. Soft tissues unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Mild joint space narrowing. No fracture.

documents.title: Sports Medicine Note
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Orthopedics & Sports Medicine - visit 04/25/2022

Washington, Tammy. 53 yo F (DOB 4/9/1969) Ref: PCP.
CC: R knee pain x3 mo.
Hx: gradual onset, worse with activity incl new walking program, eases with rest. No injury. DM, acanthosis nigricans recently dx by derm.
Meds: metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin. NKDA.
Exam: BMI 34. R knee: no erythema, no warmth. Point tenderness at the medial tibial condyle just below the joint line. ROM full. Resisted knee flexion reproduces pain. Ligaments stable.
XR R knee: mild joint space narrowing, no fracture.
Imp: Pes anserinus pain syndrome, R.
Plan: home program for hamstring/adductor stretching and quad strengthening (handout), ice 15 min after activity, diclofenac 1% gel up to QID prn. Keep walking, flatter routes for now. F/u prn.

documents.title: Sports medicine letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sports med note 4/25 reviewed: pes anserinus pain R knee, x-ray mild joint space narrowing, no fracture. Home exercises, ice, diclofenac gel prn. Added to problem and med lists. No action needed from us.

Exam date: 06/02/2022
Patient: Tammy Washington

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subjective
Fasting labs drawn this morning. Knee much better since sports med visit, doing the stretches most nights, uses the gel now and then. Walking 3-4 days a week.
New complaint: burning and tingling in the LEFT foot for about 2 months, worse at night and when she's been on her feet a long time (weekend errands). Right foot fine. No injury. She already has a follow-up booked with the same sports medicine office next month and wants them to look at it then.
Taking meds. No lows.

Objective
Vitals reviewed.
Feet: skin intact, no calluses or ulcers, DP/PT 2+ bilaterally, monofilament intact at all sites both feet, vibration intact.
Knee: no effusion.

Labs today: A1c 7.8 (from 8.5), fasting glucose 162. LDL 130, TG 250, HDL 40, TC 210. Cr normal. Urine albumin normal.

Assessment / Plan
T2DM - A1c improving with diet and walking. Continue metformin 1000 BID.
L foot burning/tingling - one-sided, normal sensory exam, does not look like diabetic neuropathy. Fine to have sports med look at it as planned; let me know what they say.
Pes anserinus pain R - improving.
HTN, mixed HLD - continue lisinopril, atorvastatin.
Return 4-5 months.

documents.title: Lab update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your A1c came down from 8.5 to 7.8. That is real progress from the walking and food changes. LDL 130 and triglycerides 250. Kidney and urine tests normal. Same plan, see you in December.

conditions.label: Tarsal tunnel syndrome, left lower limb

documents.title: foot doctor visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw the sports medicine doctor yesterday about my left foot. She said it's tarsal tunnel syndrome, a nerve getting squeezed by the inside of the ankle. She tapped there and it zinged down my foot. Bending my foot up made it worse. She wants me in supportive shoes with arch inserts and to take breaks from standing. No new meds. Just letting you know!

documents.title: RE: foot doctor visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the update, Tammy. I added tarsal tunnel syndrome on the left to your chart. The inserts and breaks are the right first step. If the numbness spreads, you get weakness, or it isn't easing in a few months, let me know.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Vaccines per PCP standing orders: flu (L deltoid), bivalent COVID booster (R deltoid), PCV20 (L deltoid, separate site) given her diabetes, Shingrix #1 (R deltoid, separate site). Screening questions negative. VIS sheets given. Observed 15 min, tolerated well. Told to expect a sore arm and maybe feeling tired tomorrow from the Shingrix. Shingrix #2 due in 2-6 months - booked for January.

conditions.label: Pes anserinus bursitis of right knee

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: R side belly discomfort, DM f/u

HPI: Several weeks of a mild ache on the right side under the ribs, comes and goes, not tied to meals that she can tell. No nausea, vomiting, fever, weight loss, change in stools, dark urine. No alcohol. Gallbladder out 2014. Knee pain gone. Foot better with the inserts. Admits walking fell off once it got cold and dark and eating has been irregular at work.

Exam: vitals as recorded. Abd obese, soft, minimally tender RUQ, liver edge hard to assess with habitus, no rebound, no guarding. No jaundice.

A/P:
1. RUQ discomfort - CMP today. Possibly fatty liver given her metabolic picture. Will refer to GI depending on liver tests.
2. T2DM - A1c today.
3. Mixed HLD - lipids today.
4. Pes anserinus pain R knee - resolved. Off the diclofenac gel.
5. Tarsal tunnel L - improving with inserts.
6. HTN - BP above goal again; continue lisinopril.

Shingrix #2 in January. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Liver tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Tammy, your liver enzymes are mildly elevated (AST 52, ALT 63; other liver tests normal). In someone with diabetes and high triglycerides the most common cause is fat building up in the liver, but I'd like a GI specialist to see you to sort it out properly, with the discomfort you've had. The referral is in, and they had an opening on the 28th.

A1c 7.9, about the same. LDL is up to 158 and triglycerides 260. Please make sure you're taking the atorvastatin every day.
